html:
The Yanktonai are one of the seven council fires of the Sioux (the Oceti Sakowin), grouped with the Yankton as the middle division between the eastern Dakota and the western Lakota.

In the 1600s they lived around the headwaters of the Mississippi and the lakes of Minnesota. Pressed by the Ojibwe, who had guns from the French fur trade, they moved west in the 1700s to the prairies of eastern North and South Dakota, between the Red River and the Missouri. They hunted bison and also kept some farming. The Assiniboine are thought to have split from them before European contact.

Their descendants live today on the Standing Rock, Crow Creek, Fort Peck and Spirit Lake reservations.
